2.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Present application has been preferred with the prayer to quash the chargesheet dated 26.04.2025 and cognizance/summoning order dated 14.05.2025 passed in Case No.433 of 2025 (State Vs. Jitendra), arising out of Case Crime no. 99 of 2025, under Sections 316(2), 351(3), 318(4)
BNS, P.S.- Gabhana, District Aligarh, pending in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate-Ist,
Aligarh.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of applicant has challenged the impugned chargesheet along with cognizance/summoning order precisely on the ground that Sections 316(2) and 318(4) BNS cannot go together in the same breath as per the proposition of law settled by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in 2024 10 SCC 690.

entities.text: Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in 2024 10 SCC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The relevant portion of the said judgment is being reproduced hereinbelow:- "38.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In our view, the plain reading of the complaint fails to spell out any of the aforesaid ingredients noted above.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: We may only say, with a view to clear a serious misconception of law in the mind of the police as well as the courts below, that if it is a case of the complainant that offence of criminal breach of trust as defined under Section 405 IPC, punishable under Section 406 IPC, is committed by the accused, then in the same breath it cannot be said that the accused has also committed the offence of cheating as defined and explained in Section 415 IPC, punishable under Section 420 IPC. 41.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The distinction between mere breach of contract and the offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating is a fine one.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In case of cheating, the intention of the accused at the time of inducement should be looked into which may be judged by a subsequent conduct, but for this, the subsequent conduct is not the sole test.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Mere breach of contract cannot give rise to a criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right from the beginning of the transaction i.e. the time when the offence is said to have been committed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, it is this intention, which is the gist of the offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 43. There is a distinction between criminal breach of trust and cheating.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: For cheating, criminal intention is necessary at the time of making a false or misleading representation i.e. since inception.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In criminal breach of trust, mere proof of entrustment is sufficient.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thus, in case of criminal breach of trust, the offender is lawfully entrusted with the property, and he dishonestly misappropriated the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Whereas, in case of cheating, the offender fraudulently or dishonestly induces a person by deceiving him to deliver any property.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In such a situation, both the offences cannot co-exist simultaneously.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 55. It is high time that the police officers across the country are imparted proper training in law so as to understand the fine distinction between the offence of cheating vis-vis criminal breach of trust.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Both offences are independent and distinct.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The two offences cannot coexist simultaneously in the same set of facts.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: They are antithetical to each other.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The two provisions of IPC (now BNS, 2023) are not twins that they cannot survive without each other."
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, going through the record of the case and the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Delhi Race Club (Supra), it is crystal clear that both the sections i.e. Sections 316(2) and 318(4) BNS cannot go in the same breath and as such, cognizance/summoning order dated 14.05.2025 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate-Ist,
Aligarh in Case No.433 of 2025 (State Vs. Jitendra), arising out of Case Crime no. 99 of 2025, under Sections 316(2), 351(3), 318(4) BNS, P.S.- Gabhana, District,
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: is quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jitendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Matter is hereby remitted back to learned Judicial Magistrate-Ist, Aligarh for passing fresh order of taking cognizance of offence, if required, in light of the proposition of law settled by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Delhi Race Club (supra).
6. Accordingly, the instant application stands allowed in part.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The distinction between mere breach of contract and the offence of criminal breach of trust and cheating is a fine one.
In case of cheating, the intention of the accused at the time of inducement should be looked into which may be judged by a subsequent conduct, but for this, the subsequent conduct is not the sole test.
Mere breach of contract cannot give rise to a criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right from the beginning of the transaction i.e. the time when the offence is said to have been committed.
43. There is a distinction between criminal breach of trust and cheating.
Whereas, in case of cheating, the offender fraudulently or dishonestly induces a person by deceiving him to deliver any property.
In such a situation, both the offences cannot co-exist simultaneously.
Both offences are independent and distinct.
The two offences cannot coexist simultaneously in the same set of facts.
They are antithetical to each other.
